{{Short description|Family of sets indexed by ordinal numbers}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically [[set theory]], a '''cumulative hierarchy''' is a family of [[set (mathematics)|sets]] <math>W_\alpha</math> indexed by [[ordinal number|ordinals]] <math>\alpha</math> such that

* <math>W_\alpha \subseteq W_{\alpha + 1}</math>
* If <math>\lambda</math> is a [[limit ordinal]], then <math display="inline">W_\lambda = \bigcup_{\alpha < \lambda} W_{\alpha}</math>

Some authors additionally require that <math>W_{\alpha + 1} \subseteq \mathcal P(W_\alpha)</math>.{{cn|reason=Give an example citation for each additional requirements.|date=June 2019}}

The [[Union (set theory)|union]] <math display="inline">W = \bigcup_{\alpha \in \mathrm{On}} W_\alpha</math> of the sets of a cumulative hierarchy is often used as a model of set theory.{{cn|date=June 2019}}

The phrase "the cumulative hierarchy" usually refers to the [[von Neumann hierarchy]], which has <math>W_{\alpha + 1} = \mathcal P(W_\alpha)</math>.

==Reflection principle==
A cumulative hierarchy satisfies a form of the [[reflection principle]]: any [[Well-formed formula|formula]] in the language of set theory that holds in the union <math>W</math> of the hierarchy also holds in some stages <math>W_\alpha</math>.

==Examples==
* The von Neumann universe is built from a cumulative hierarchy <math>\mathrm{V}_\alpha</math>.
*The sets <math>\mathrm{L}_\alpha</math> of the [[constructible universe]] form a cumulative hierarchy.
*The [[Boolean-valued model]]s constructed by [[Forcing (mathematics)|forcing]] are built using a cumulative hierarchy.
*The [[well-founded set]]s in a model of set theory (possibly not satisfying the [[axiom of foundation]]) form a cumulative hierarchy whose union satisfies the axiom of foundation.
